doc.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023

title: Transcriptions of his solos and Dizzy's reaction to his own
summary: Sandoval says he could play transcriptions as a sight reader and tells how Dizzy called a transcription of his own solo impossible.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: A couple of more questions. Back to your improvising. Have you — I know I’ve seen transcriptions of your solos. And I wonder if, you probably have as well, are you able to play them if you wanted to after they’ve been written out? © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-

Oh. Yeah. I used to be a very good sight reader you know. And as I practiced it, yeah, I used to be able to do it. It’s always — you know what, I’ll never forget, one time that I get together with Dizzy after traveling to somewhere. I copied one of the transcriptions of one of his solos. And I said, and I showed it to him, I said, “Diz, look at this man.” And he said, “What the heck is that?” I said, “It’s something transcribed, a kind of trumpet solo. You think that’s possible to play?” He said, “Hell no, that’s impossible.” I said, “Diz, that was your solo. That was your solo, man.” He said, “No kidding.”
But when you just a couple of minutes ago you were doing the solfeggio and you were moving your — you weren’t playing the piano, you were moving your trumpet fingers. Okay. Do you think that —
